title: docs(qa): 18.0 sweep round 11 — the walled pass of QA round 3: RUNNER's walled boot under serve, and eight items' producers, recipes and refusals
body:
Refs #24579
Clause-②: no

Round 11 of the 18.0 release sweep's wave anchor (#24579), claim `6284734380`. This is the walled pass of QA round 3: QA record #24783's checklist-accuracy findings F1 to F8, the round-3 summary's (`6284472874`) §1 re-point and §6 environment fact, and `access-security.scope-depth-asymmetry`'s pin. Only checklist text changes: `RUNNER.md` (which carries no revision) and 8 items in 5 area files, each with one `revision` bump and one `history` row. No product code, test, pin or changeset text changed.

Base `46bb5e3e54`. The edits are commits `79222a3b2e` (RUNNER) and `8a5a8b0660` (area files). `origin/main` then moved to `a43405d596` (#24743, one `.claude` skill reference, disjoint), merged at `423d2726dc`. Each history row's `ref` is written as this branch's name and is filled with this PR's number in one later commit that changes only those 8 strings.

Each finding was re-read in the code at the base before it was written. Where the code disagreed with the finding, the finding was not applied as written, and the table says so.

## RUNNER.md

| place | old → new | code anchor read at `46bb5e3e54` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| "A walled boot is a fixture of its own", the prerequisites sentence (F2) | "Each prerequisite below refuses the boot with a FATAL naming itself" → "Through `os dev`, each prerequisite below refuses …" (QA run #24783 measured all three). Round 10's first sentence, the 18.0.0 / `next.5` attribution, is unchanged. | `os dev` spawns `serve --dev`; `resolveAuthSecret()` in `packages/core/src/stack-auth.ts` falls back to `DEV_AUTH_SECRET_FALLBACK` on a development boot |
| same entry, new paragraph (F2) | A bare `os serve` in production mode judges none of the three until `OS_AUTH_SECRET` resolves. Without it AuthPlugin is skipped and the boot comes up `DEGRADED: missing core services: auth`, not FATAL. It also needs a stable encryption key. | `resolvePlatformAuthComposition()` (reason `no-secret`); the `⚠ AuthPlugin skipped` branch in `serve.ts`, with the multi-org runtime load inside that branch's composing arm; the owner-email throw in `AuthPlugin.init()`; `assertWalledMembershipPolicyDeclared()` skips a kernel with no `auth` service; `printServerReady()` prints the DEGRADED line; `LocalCryptoProvider`'s "Refusing to start in production without a stable encryption key" |
| same entry, prerequisite 1 (F2) | "a scratch app that does" → a full copy of `examples/app-showcase` (with `src/`), every dependency as `link:` plus `@objectstack/organizations`, `pnpm install --ignore-workspace`. A config that only re-exports the showcase does not boot. | the OpenAPI connector's `spec: './src/system/connectors/status-openapi.json'` (`examples/app-showcase/src/system/connectors/index.ts`) resolves against the package root at materialization |
| same entry, new paragraph (F2) | Walled personas come from `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/create-user`: sign-up answers 403 `SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED`, and under `invite-only` each created user lands with `membershipCreated: false`. | `decideAudienceAdmission()` (`audience-posture.ts`); `runAdminCreateUser()`; `reconcileMembership()` answers `policy-skip` under `invite-only` |
| new environment fact, after the `ss` entry (round-3 §6) | A SIGTERM to the `pnpm` wrapper leaves the `serve` grandchild listening. Start with `setsid`, read the group id from the listener, and stop the process group. | `os dev`'s SIGTERM handler forwards to its child only (`beginShutdown()` of `ServeRestartCoordinator`, `packages/cli/src/utils/dev-restart.ts`). Measured here with a stand-in tree under `pnpm -C examples/app-showcase exec`: two seconds after a SIGTERM to pnpm the child still answered 200, and a SIGTERM to the group stopped all four processes. It also measured that a backgrounded `setsid` forks, so `$!` is not the group id. |

**Not applied as written:** the dispatch's "bare `os serve` / `os start`". `os start` hands its `serve` child an auth secret (its flag, the environment, or a persisted `auth-secret` file) and sets `OS_CRYPTO_AUTOKEY` (`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts`). So the secret skip is `serve`'s alone. The entry says this was read from the code and not booted.

The line also gives the two measured refusals. | `security-plugin.ts#denyTenantPlacement` ("outside the caller's organization scope"); ADR-0090 D12 (c) in `delegated-admin-gate.ts#organizationBoundaryFailure` (`manage_metadata` is `scope: 'platform'` in `capabilities.ts`); `wall-environment-metadata-refusal.dogfood.test.ts#boot` |

The scratch `sys_webhook` needs `definition_json` (required) and a lower-case `method`. | `auto-enqueuer.ts` `admitsOrganization` (`deploymentWide` first); `wall-declared-webhook-deployment-wide.dogfood.test.ts` (its "[ruling A] … a declared webhook is deployment-wide" describe, run under both postures); `sys-webhook.object.ts` (`definition_json` `required: true`, `Field.select` lower-cases the options) |

QA run #24783 measured the order on both postures. | `actions.ts#handleActionActivationWrite` (both authority tiers before shape, body and lookup) |

The new knownGap says that no HTTP door sets the lock. | `sys-setting.object.ts` `apiMethods: ['get', 'list']` (an update answers 405); `settings-service.ts#setMany` takes a key-to-value patch and never writes `locked` |

The new line says what the three dogfood suites assert and when `automated` may return. The item is now Tier 2. | the three suites never drive the manager, executive or ops personas, or `showcase_inquiry` (read at the base) |

**F1: nothing recorded.** No ledger field marks an item as walled. The 21 item keys used across the area files hold no tag and no `walled` marker. `scripts/checklist-select.mjs` has no `walled` selector key, so `walled:isolated+group` resolves to 0 items. The three items matched on words in free text: `lead_walled` in `knownGaps[1]` and `automated.ref`; "boot showcase isolated" in `steps[0]`; "isolated scratch file DB" in `knownGaps[0]`. The 14-item list was the runner's own selection.

**Governing-text decision (F3).** `acceptance[0]` is aligned, citing ADR-0123 D2 and ADR-0105 D2, which state the `group` answer. `acceptance[4]` is left as written, because no ADR states it, and `knownGaps[3]` names the question. #24784 is named in `knownGaps[4]`.

## Left alone, and why

- `platform-core.v18-boot-refusals` and `areas/cli.json`: PR #24681 (open) edits them, and the claim excludes them.
- `access-security.grant-table-write-contract` and `access-security.parent-and-organization-write-guards`: both carry round 10's walled line, with the same "each one absent refuses the boot naming itself" sentence. They are outside this claim's file surface, so they still read the old way, and the card report names them.
- `access-security.platform-owner-email-anchor` and `attachments-storage.chunked-upload-integrity`: both cite the RUNNER entry but carry no refusal sentence.
- `no-active-org-session-semantics`'s `blocked` marker, and its `acceptance[1]`, `[4]` to `[6]`: the marker still holds (the stock showcase cannot run any clause). The clauses have no governing text to align them to.
- History rows of earlier revisions: history is append-only.

PR #24681 touches `platform-core.json` (item `v18-boot-refusals` only) and `cli.json`, so it shares no item with this PR, and no path here is routed to the `os-regen` driver.

## How the edits were made

The area files went through a span-recording editor. It applies each declared op twice, once to the parsed item and once to the item's own text span, and then asserts four things:
1. the new document equals the old one with the ops applied (key order included);
2. every other item and top-level key is value-equal to before;
3. the changed leaf paths are exactly the declared fields plus `revision` plus one new `history` row;
4. the text outside the edited items is byte-identical.

Its changed-path report matched the declarations for all 8 items.

## Acceptance notes

- QA run #24783 F3 explains the admin-created user's missing membership as ADR-0093 D1 `no-target-org`. At the base, `invite-only` answers `policy-skip` before any organization is looked at (`reconcileMembership()`). This corrects the record's explanation and is noted here, not filed.
- No changeset: `docs/qa/**` ships in no package. The root package is private, and none of the 73 published manifests names `docs/qa` in `files[]` (control: all 73 name `dist`). Hence `skip-changeset`.
